## Report

The claim is well-supported by high-quality evidence. The pivotal study is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial (n=120) published in the *New England Journal of Medicine* (2017), which found that add-on cannabidiol (CBD, as the pharmaceutical formulation later branded Epidiolex) significantly reduced convulsive seizure frequency over 14 weeks in children/young adults with drug-resistant Dravet syndrome, though it also increased adverse events like diarrhea, vomiting, fatigue, and elevated liver enzymes (https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa1611618).

A second randomized trial (JAMA Neurology, 2020) tested two CBD doses against placebo and again found both significantly reduced convulsive seizures compared to placebo, establishing a dose-response relationship (https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jamaneurology/fullarticle/2762458).

Long-term open-label extension data (Epilepsia, 2018 and 2021) tracking patients for over 150 weeks showed sustained, clinically meaningful seizure reductions with an acceptable long-term safety profile, though liver enzyme monitoring and interaction with valproate/clobazam remain a concern (https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1111/epi.14628).

Based on this randomized and long-term evidence, the FDA approved Epidiolex (purified CBD) in 2018 specifically for seizures associated with Dravet syndrome, Lennox-Gastaut syndrome, and tuberous sclerosis complex—the only cannabis-derived drug with this regulatory approval (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2018/210365lbl.pdf).

**Conclusion:** Your sister's belief is accurate and reflects the scientific consensus. Multiple randomized controlled trials, replicated results, and long-term follow-up data consistently show that add-on pharmaceutical-grade CBD reduces convulsive seizure frequency in Dravet syndrome, leading to FDA approval. This applies specifically to purified, prescription CBD (Epidiolex)—not necessarily over-the-counter CBD products, which are unregulated and untested for this purpose.
